name: Study Ledger
summary: Warm paper, black ink, one oxblood accent, a heavy rule over every page. A reader's guide that shows its sourcing: every claim carries a mark for how well it is known, as a rule style and a word, and the mark says what to do with the claim.

for: pages built on quotations, citations or claims of uneven reliability
catalogues of works with a date for each
not_for: pages with no claims to grade

type.display: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, "Book Antiqua", Georgia, serif
type.text: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, "Book Antiqua", Georgia, serif

shape.note: system fonts only; labels and metadata in system sans at 13px or more; hard offset shadows, no blur

signature.name: the shelf
signature.rule: One flat book per work, stacked in a column per year along a single shelf: the width of the picture is the span of years, the height of a column is how many books that year. One ink colour; the accent marks the works the page recommends, and the caption says so. It must fit the phone width with a caption and a link to the full list, never a hidden sideways scroller.
signature.carries: how many works exist, in which years they were published, and which ones the page recommends
signature.derived_from: data/works.json: one rectangle per work, the page text prints the same count and years

motifs.use: every quotation or claim whose source varies
motifs.rule: A left rule whose style is the mark: solid = book named but unchecked, dashed = widely attributed, dotted = no source known, double accent = credited to someone else. Always with the word, and each mark is written as an action (say 'attributed to', do not quote, do not attribute). The legend is the filter: one control, not a legend plus a repeat of it. Counts are printed from the data.
The year sits in the left margin in the accent colour, repeated years collapse to a dot, so the list reads as a ledger.
A 2px ink border and a hard offset shadow (no blur); the whole card is the link target.

never: promoting a quote because it is popular
a contact form with nowhere to post
a fixed footer over the content
an unlabelled image whose licence is unknown (say so in the footer)
a top tier named as if verified when no source has been checked (name it 'unchecked' until a page is)
'could not find it' wording where no search was made (say 'not yet searched for')
a licence line that implies the photographs and quoted words are covered by the site's licence

provenance.source_run: SolutionsAsService/ThomasSowell, Adaptive Full run bounded to one panel round (Krug, Debord, Cairo); see its DESIGN-LOG.md
measured: Mobile Floor 12 of 12 at 360, 390 and 430px on all 5 pages, re-run after each change set
contrast preset n:0 on all pages; lowest measured pair 5.04:1 light, 6.66:1 dark
all printed figures equal the data files; the shelf has one rect per work
deep links, filters and hash fallbacks verified in a real browser; no-JS verified
open: one panel round; S1 and S2 not met
every quotation unchecked against a printed page; biography from general knowledge
the shelf is small at 390px (about 10px blocks); a two-row phone layout was not tried
no inclusion seat; not shown on a real phone
